Westmoreland Resources can now mine themselves, grant another option, or sublease to one or more firms for the sale of the 300 million tons of coal. However, the option or sublease would have to be approved by the Crow tribe and the Secretary of the Interior. If an option or sublease is granted for the sale of coal for use in a coal conversion or mine mouth generating facility to be located upon or within 50 miles of the exterior boundaries of the diminished Crow Indian Reservation, approval of such sale must be given by the Crow Tribe.
COAL RESOURCES INVOLVED
Most of the minable coal on the leases is contained in the Robinson and the Rosebud-McKay coal seams. Westmoreland Resources has estimated that 350 million and 850 million tons of coal underlie Tracts II and III respectively. At current market conditions Westmoreland Resources estimates that 234 and 592 million tons for Tracts II and III, respectively, are economically recoverable.
The coal is subbituminous "B" grade with about a 8,450 Btu/1b heating value. Sulfur content for both coal seams averages 0.73 percent.
Chapter II contains detailed information concerning the coal seams physical and chemical analysis and trace element concentrations.
